newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts eager to punch through 114-31 high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts eager to punch through 114-31 high.

text.p: September gilt futures on LIFFE will aim to take out the contract high at 114-31 on Wednesday and head for levels not seen since February 1994, technical analysts said.
A budget that disappoints the market however, could curb any significant charge higher, they said.
"It's budget day today so it's all a bit volatile," said David Wood, independent technical analyst near London. "If we are going to go through to new highs we're going to do it on this run up."
Gilts were quoted at 114-21, up 1/32 from Tuesday.
Gilts hit the contract high on May 9.
Wood said the next objective past the 115-00 area was 115-15, projections from hourly ranges and the high on February 25, 1994 on weekly continuation charts.

Richard Adcock, manager of technical research at HSBC Futures in London, was surprised by gilts' performance on Tuesday. A late rally pushed gilts through an initial barrier at 114-19 to a 114-20 close, just off the day's high at 114-23.
"This signals attempts to break through the recent 114-31 high with successful moves opening the way for moves to 116-00," he said in a research note.
Wood said initial support this session lay around 114-18,19, the highs from June 30 and June 27.

"But the bulk of the support comes in at 114-12/10," he said, noting congestion at these levels. He put a further buffer at 114-06 and a stronger barrier at 114-02. Daily charts show this level as the high from June 26.
At the short end, December short sterling futures were quoted at 92.80 at 0715 GMT, up three basis points from Tuesday's pit settlement.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown delivers his first budget at 1430 GMT.
